titulo: Quiz — Before you fly, and the border
subtitulo: One arrival, start to finish: the camera, the three questions, and a SIM card that actually works
introPt: Quiz time. A British couple land at Madrid-Barajas at half past seven in the morning, jet-lagged and phoneless. In the next four minutes they'll be photographed, fingerprinted, asked three questions, and sold a SIM card. Listen as many times as you like, then answer.
cenario: Arrivals at a Spanish airport: the EES biometric registration, the three border questions with the booking held up as proof, and then the phone shop in the arrivals hall.

dialogo.es: Mire a la cámara, por favor. Ahora los cuatro dedos aquí.
dialogo.pinyin: MEE-reh ah lah KAH-mah-rah, por fah-BOR. ah-OH-rah lohs KWAH-troh DEH-dhohs ah-KEE
dialogo.pt: — Look at the camera, please. Now four fingers here.

dialogo.es: Me alojo en el hotel Rialto, en Madrid. Aquí tiene la reserva.
dialogo.pinyin: meh ah-LOH-khoh en el oh-TEL ree-AHL-toh, en mah-DREEDH. ah-KEE TYEH-neh lah rreh-SEHR-bah
dialogo.pt: — I'm staying at the Hotel Rialto, in Madrid. Here's the booking. (phone held up)

dialogo.es: Muy bien. Que tenga buen viaje.
dialogo.pinyin: mwee byen. keh TEN-gah bwen BYAH-kheh
dialogo.pt: — Very good. Have a good trip.

dialogo.pinyin: OH-lah. TYEH-nen tar-KHEH-tahs seem deh preh-PAH-goh
dialogo.pt: — Hello. Do you have prepaid SIM cards? (at the phone shop)

dialogo.es: Sí. ¿Me deja el pasaporte, por favor?
dialogo.pinyin: see. meh DEH-khah el pah-sah-POR-teh, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Yes. Can I have your passport, please? (the assistant)

dialogo.es: Aquí tiene. Quiero una tarjeta SIM de prepago, solo datos.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-KEE TYEH-neh. KYEH-roh OO-nah tar-KHEH-tah seem deh preh-PAH-goh, SOH-loh DAH-tohs
dialogo.pt: — Here you are. I'd like a prepaid SIM, data only.

dialogo.es: ¿Me la puede activar aquí, por favor?
dialogo.pinyin: meh lah PWEH-dheh ak-tee-BAR ah-KEE, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Can you activate it for me here, please?

perguntas.es: The officer says 'Mire a la cámara' and then asks for four fingers. What is she doing?
perguntas.pergunta: The officer says 'Mire a la cámara' and then asks for four fingers. What is she doing?
opcoes: Registering him on the EES system — the biometric record that replaced the passport stamp
Checking his ETIAS authorisation
Taking a security photo because he was picked at random
Charging him for a visa on arrival
perguntas.pt: That's EES. Since April 2026 it replaces the stamp across 29 countries: face photo plus four fingerprints on the first crossing, about four minutes. It's free, and after the first time it's quick.
perguntas.explica: That's EES. Since April 2026 it replaces the stamp across 29 countries: face photo plus four fingerprints on the first crossing, about four minutes. It's free, and after the first time it's quick.

perguntas.es: 'Diez días.' How long is he staying?
perguntas.pergunta: 'Diez días.' How long is he staying?
opcoes: Two days
Ten days
Twelve days
Two hundred days
perguntas.pt: 'Diez' is ten, and that 'z' is the 'th' of 'think' — DYETH. It's the sound that separates 'diez' from 'doce' (twelve) on a noisy bar bill, which is why it's worth banking on day one.
perguntas.explica: 'Diez' is ten, and that 'z' is the 'th' of 'think' — DYETH. It's the sound that separates 'diez' from 'doce' (twelve) on a noisy bar bill, which is why it's worth banking on day one.

perguntas.es: After naming his hotel he says 'Aquí tiene la reserva.' Why does that end the conversation?
perguntas.pergunta: After naming his hotel he says 'Aquí tiene la reserva.' Why does that end the conversation?
opcoes: Because it's a legal formula officers have to accept
Because he's showing the booking — the artefact does the arguing, not the sentence
Because it means 'I have nothing to declare'
Because it's the polite way to end any exchange in Spain
perguntas.pt: 'Aquí tiene' = 'here you are'. Have the booking already open on your phone before you reach the desk. Showing is faster and safer than improvising a longer sentence — and you're never the person holding up the queue.
perguntas.explica: 'Aquí tiene' = 'here you are'. Have the booking already open on your phone before you reach the desk. Showing is faster and safer than improvising a longer sentence — and you're never the person holding up the queue.

perguntas.es: At the phone shop the assistant asks for his passport. Is that normal?
perguntas.pergunta: At the phone shop the assistant asks for his passport. Is that normal?
opcoes: No — walk out, that's a scam
Only if you're paying in cash
Yes — Spanish prepaid SIMs are registered to a document, and they need the physical passport
Yes, but a photo of it on your phone is always accepted
perguntas.pt: Prepaid SIMs in Spain must be registered against an ID document at the point of sale, and shops routinely refuse a photo or a scan. Take the passport itself — or buy and test an eSIM at home and skip the counter entirely.
perguntas.explica: Prepaid SIMs in Spain must be registered against an ID document at the point of sale, and shops routinely refuse a photo or a scan. Take the passport itself — or buy and test an eSIM at home and skip the counter entirely.

perguntas.es: Three weeks before the trip, a website offers to sell you an ETIAS for €59, 'processed in 24 hours'. What do you do?
perguntas.pergunta: Three weeks before the trip, a website offers to sell you an ETIAS for €59, 'processed in 24 hours'. What do you do?
opcoes: Buy it — you can't board without one
Nothing. There is no open ETIAS application portal, so anyone selling one today is running a scam
Buy the cheapest one you can find, since they're all the same
Ask your airline to apply on your behalf
perguntas.pt: ETIAS has been announced at €20 and repeatedly postponed; as of summer 2026 there is no portal open. There's exactly one official EU site. Check it about 60 days before you fly and ignore everything else.
perguntas.explica: ETIAS has been announced at €20 and repeatedly postponed; as of summer 2026 there is no portal open. There's exactly one official EU site. Check it about 60 days before you fly and ignore everything else.

perguntas.es: You spent 80 days in Spain in the last six months and you'd like to go back next week. How does the 90/180 rule work?
perguntas.pergunta: You spent 80 days in Spain in the last six months and you'd like to go back next week. How does the 90/180 rule work?
opcoes: You get a fresh 90 days on 1 January, so it depends on the calendar year
The window rolls: count back 180 days from any given day, so you have around 10 days left — and arrival and departure days both count
Only complete days count, so short trips are free
Owning property in Spain gives you extra days
perguntas.pt: Ninety days in any rolling 180 — no January reset, day of entry and day of exit both count, and since EES the total is computed automatically. Overstaying risks a ban of up to three years. And no: a villa in Marbella buys you nothing.
perguntas.explica: Ninety days in any rolling 180 — no January reset, day of entry and day of exit both count, and since EES the total is computed automatically. Overstaying risks a ban of up to three years. And no: a villa in Marbella buys you nothing.
